terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; comparative celerior, superlative celerrimus
evidence: Ov. Tr. 3.12.20: celerī volvitur orbe trochus
Plaut. Trin. 4.3.1: face tē properē celerem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word for speed, of people, animals, ships and thoughts, the opposite of tardus; celeriter, quickly (see quickly), celeritās, speed (see speed).
Of speed of movement, in animals and runners above all: the dolphin, the hare, the hound.

terms.register: chiefly poetic in this sense (Verg., Ov.)
evidence: Lewis & Short: of waters, winds and fire
terms.comment: First tearing, seizing (of fire and heat); then rushing along, of rivers, winds and horses. Not the everyday word for a fast person (that is celer).

phrases.latin: vēlōcissimum omnium animālium, nōn sōlum marīnōrum, est delphīnus
phrases.english: the fastest of all animals, not only of the sea, is the dolphin

phrases.latin: cum vēnātōrem celerī pede fugeret lepus
phrases.english: when a hare was running from a hunter on swift feet
